content:
We've heard numerous rumors about Apple's next-generation iPad mini, including the adoption of an OLED display and improved water resistance.

A new leak today suggests that the upcoming iPad mini will be equipped with the powerful A20 Pro chip.

MacRumors discovered information about the new iPad mini in Apple's code today, including what appears to be a product icon for the device.

The icon shows that the overall design of the new iPad mini will be largely similar to the current model. However, the camera has been moved from the top bezel to one side in landscape orientation, aligning with Apple's other iPad models. There is also a small speaker grille at the top of the display, similar to the iPhone.

The code also shows that the new iPad mini will feature the A20 Pro chip, the same chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro series launched last week. The current iPad mini, which went on sale in October 2024, uses Apple's A17 Pro chip.

According to Mark Gurman, the new iPad mini is expected to go on sale before the end of October. In addition to the above changes, the new iPad mini is reportedly set to offer improved water resistance and a new speaker system.

For more details, refer to our comprehensive roundup of expected features for the new iPad mini.

Another separate report today also revealed details about the next-generation entry-level iPad, including the A19 chip, 8GB of memory, and Apple's N1 and C1X connectivity chips.
